headline: Jio’s Debut Puts It Second Behind Reliance
deck: Jio Platforms’ listing followed what TechCrunch described as India’s largest and most subscribed initial public offering.
body: Jio Platforms made its market debut after raising $3.2 billion in what TechCrunch described as India’s largest and most subscribed IPO, which it said attracted more than $77 billion in investor bids. This follows the paper’s 28 October coverage of the offering. [E1][E2]

Shares opened at ₹1,358, against an IPO price of ₹1,119. TechCrunch described the debut as a 21% gain, while 5paisa put the premium at 21.36%, a difference in the reports’ stated percentage. [E1][E3][E8]
TechCrunch valued Jio at about ₹12.5 trillion after the debut, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company behind Reliance Industries, which it put at about ₹16 trillion. [E4]
TechCrunch said the offer ran from 21 to 22 October. [E5]
More than 13.8 million people applied for shares, TechCrunch reported. [E6]
Jio made ₹300.5 billion in profit on revenue of ₹1.47 trillion in the fiscal year ended March 2026, with both figures up about 15% from a year earlier, TechCrunch reported. [E7]
5paisa said the offering opened on 21 October and closed on 23 October, differing from TechCrunch’s stated closing date. [E9]

The reports also differ on overall subscription: TechCrunch cited bids for 22.19 times the shares on sale, while 5paisa put it at 21.36 times and said qualified institutional buyers subscribed 67.15 times their allocation. [E5][E10]
